entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Marcus Cocceius Nerva was a Roman consul and senator who played a crucial role in the late Republic, serving as consul in 36 BC alongside Lucius Gellius Poplicola. Nerva was a member of the influential Cocceian family, which had ties to the Populares faction, and was known for his involvement in the political machinations of the time. As a senator, he was a key figure in the struggles between the Optimates and the Populares, and his family's connections to Marcus Antonius, the leader of the Populares, provided him with a significant amount of influence and power. Nerva's significance lies in his role as a mediator between the two factions, and his eventual support of Augustus, the future emperor, helped to bring stability to the Roman Republic. Despite his importance, Nerva's life and legacy are relatively well-documented, and his impact on the course of Roman history is still studied by historians today.
